bss.topic: República Velha: café com leite e coronelismo

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Em que ano foi proclamada a República no Brasil?
questions.hint: Foi no fim do século XIX, um ano depois da abolição da escravidão.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Que acontecimento marcou o fim da República Velha?
questions.hint: Pense no ano em que esse período terminou.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Quais dois estados se revezavam no poder na política do café com leite?
options: Rio Grande do Sul e Santa Catarina
questions.hint: Um era o maior produtor de café; o outro, forte na pecuária leiteira.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Na expressão “café com leite”, o “café” representa qual estado?
questions.hint: Pense no estado com as maiores plantações de café na época.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Por que São Paulo e Minas Gerais tinham tanto poder na República Velha?
options: Eram estados ricos e com muitos eleitores
questions.answer: Eram estados ricos e com muitos eleitores
questions.hint: Pense em economia e em número de votos.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Como eram chamados os grandes fazendeiros que mandavam na política das cidades do interior?
questions.hint: O nome lembra um posto militar.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: O que era o coronelismo?
options: O domínio político dos grandes fazendeiros no interior
Uma lei que protegia os trabalhadores
Um tipo de plantação de café
questions.answer: O domínio político dos grandes fazendeiros no interior
questions.hint: Pense em quem mandava nas cidades pequenas.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: O que era o voto de cabresto?
options: O eleitor era pressionado a votar no candidato do coronel
O voto era feito pelo correio
questions.answer: O eleitor era pressionado a votar no candidato do coronel
questions.hint: Cabresto é a corda usada para guiar o cavalo.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Por que era fácil para o coronel controlar os votos?
options: Porque o voto não era secreto
questions.answer: Porque o voto não era secreto
questions.hint: Pense se as outras pessoas podiam ver em quem você votava.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Como se chamava a região em que um coronel controlava os votos dos eleitores?
questions.hint: O nome compara os eleitores a um rebanho.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Pela Constituição de 1891, qual destes grupos NÃO podia votar?
options: Os homens alfabetizados acima de 21 anos
questions.hint: Pense em quem não sabia ler e escrever, a maioria da população na época.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Em que estado ficava o arraial de Canudos?
questions.hint: Ficava no sertão do Nordeste.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Quem formava a comunidade de Canudos?
options: Sertanejos pobres, guiados por um líder religioso
questions.answer: Sertanejos pobres, guiados por um líder religioso
questions.hint: Pense nas pessoas que viviam no sertão sem terra.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Como terminou a Guerra de Canudos, em 1897?
options: O arraial foi destruído pelo Exército
Canudos virou a capital do Brasil
Os moradores venceram e ficaram independentes
Houve um acordo de paz com o governo
questions.answer: O arraial foi destruído pelo Exército
questions.hint: O governo enviou várias expedições militares.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: A República Velha foi de 1889 a 1930. Quantos anos durou esse período?
questions.hint: Faça a subtração entre os dois anos.

questions.subject: bss
questions.q: Explique por que o voto secreto ajuda a combater o voto de cabresto.
questions.hint: Pense no que o coronel não conseguiria mais saber.

en.topic: Colons and semi-colons in lists; bullet points

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which punctuation mark is used to introduce a list after a complete sentence?
questions.hint: It looks like two dots, one above the other.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What is the name of this punctuation mark: ; ?
questions.hint: It is a dot above a comma.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which sentence uses a colon correctly?
options: We visited three cities: Paris, Rome and Madrid.
We: visited three cities, Paris, Rome and Madrid.
We visited three: cities, Paris, Rome and Madrid.
We visited three cities, Paris: Rome and Madrid.
questions.answer: We visited three cities: Paris, Rome and Madrid.
questions.hint: The part before the colon should make sense on its own.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Where should the colon go? "The recipe needs four ingredients flour, eggs, milk and sugar."
questions.hint: Find where the list begins.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which word should come directly before the colon? "Bring the following items a hat, sun cream and a towel."
questions.hint: The colon goes just before the list starts.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which sentence does NOT use a colon correctly?
options: There is one rule: be kind.
You will need three tools: a saw, a hammer and nails.
The shop sold two things: bread and milk.
questions.hint: A colon should not split a verb from its object.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: When should you use semi-colons to separate items in a list?
options: When the items are long or already contain commas
When the list has only two items
At the end of every sentence
questions.answer: When the items are long or already contain commas
questions.hint: Think about how to stop a list from becoming confusing.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which punctuation should fill both gaps? "On the trip we met Ana, our guide__ Leo, the driver__ and Mia, the cook."
questions.hint: Each item already has a comma inside it.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Which sentence uses semi-colons correctly in a list?
options: The team visited Leeds, in Yorkshire; Bath, in Somerset; and York, also in Yorkshire.
The team visited; Leeds, Bath and York.
The team; visited Leeds, Bath and York.
The team visited Leeds; Bath, York.
questions.answer: The team visited Leeds, in Yorkshire; Bath, in Somerset; and York, also in Yorkshire.
questions.hint: Look for the list where each item has extra information.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Why are semi-colons more helpful than commas in this list? "Our club has three groups: painters, who meet on Monday; singers, who meet on Wednesday; and dancers, who meet on Friday."
options: Semi-colons are always used with colons
questions.hint: Count the commas inside each item.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What usually comes before a list of bullet points?
options: An introductory phrase ending with a colon
questions.answer: An introductory phrase ending with a colon
questions.hint: Think about how a writer introduces the list.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: If each bullet point is a full sentence, how should it be punctuated?
options: Start with a capital letter and end with a full stop
Start with a lower-case letter and no full stop
questions.answer: Start with a capital letter and end with a full stop
questions.hint: Treat each one like a normal sentence.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: What is the most important rule when punctuating bullet points?
options: Be consistent all the way through
Use a different style for each point
questions.answer: Be consistent all the way through
questions.hint: Every point should follow the same pattern.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: A bullet list reads: "pack a torch", "bring a coat", "Water bottle." Which point breaks the pattern?
questions.hint: Check capital letters, full stops and whether each starts with a verb.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Write one sentence that uses a colon to introduce a list of three things you would take to the beach.
questions.hint: Make sure the words before the colon could be a sentence on their own.

questions.subject: en
questions.q: Explain why a writer might choose bullet points instead of writing a list inside a sentence.
questions.hint: Think about how easy it is for a reader to find information.

All words ending in "t" double it

questions.answer: The last syllable of "forget" is stressed
questions.hint: Say "for-GET" and notice which part is louder.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Which word keeps a single consonant when -ing is added, because the stress is on the first syllable?

questions.subject: en_spell

questions.hint: Count the double letters carefully.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Which is the correct spelling of "limit" + ed?
questions.hint: Is "limit" stressed at the start or the end?

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Spot the mistakes: find and fix the 5 misspelled words.
questions.answer: begining → beginning; forgeting → forgetting; admited → admitted; occured → occurred; permited → permitted
questions.hint: Check every word that ends in -ing or -ed.
questions.text: Last week our class started a big project. At the begining, I kept forgeting my notes at home. Then I admited that I needed a plan. Something surprising occured: I started to enjoy it. Our teacher permited us to work in the garden, and nobody regretted it.

questions.subject: en_spell
questions.q: Spot the mistakes: find and fix the 4 misspelled words.
questions.answer: visitting → visiting; controled → controlled; propeled → propelled; comitted → committed
questions.hint: Think about stress: double the consonant only when the last syllable is stressed.
questions.text: Tourists visitting the airfield watched as the pilots controled the small plane while strong winds propeled it forward. It was a compelling sight. The crew had comitted to landing safely, and everyone cheered when the wheels finally touched the ground.
